facts.display: 6.1-inch Super Retina XDR OLED; 6.12-inch diagonal when measured as a standard rectangle.
facts.rear_camera: 48MP Fusion main camera and 12MP Ultra Wide; the main camera also supports 2x optical-quality zoom.
facts.battery: Apple rates video playback up to 22 hours, or streamed video up to 18 hours.

iPhone 16.everyday_note: The OLED screen is suited to video and photos; the Ultra Wide camera captures more of a scene, while the main camera offers a 2x optical-quality view. Apple’s battery figure is a lab rating, not a guarantee of daily runtime.

facts.water_resistance: IP68, tested up to 6 meters for up to 30 minutes.

iPhone 16 Pro.everyday_note: The screen is in the larger 6-inch class, giving extra room for reading and video.

facts.water_resistance: IP68, tested up to 6 meters for up to 30 minutes.

iPhone 16 Pro Max.everyday_note: The largest screen in this list offers the most viewing room, though it may feel less compact in hand.

facts.display: 6.3-inch Super Retina XDR OLED with adaptive ProMotion up to 120Hz; 6.27-inch diagonal when measured as a standard rectangle.
facts.rear_camera: 48MP Dual Fusion system with a 48MP main camera and 48MP Ultra Wide; also supports 2x optical-quality telephoto framing.
facts.battery: Apple rates video playback up to 30 hours, or streamed video up to 27 hours.
facts.water_resistance: IP68, tested up to 6 meters for up to 30 minutes.

iPhone 17.everyday_note: The 120Hz display can make scrolling feel smoother, and the 48MP Ultra Wide can capture more detail in wide scenes. Center Stage helps keep people framed during supported video calls. Apple’s battery figure is a lab rating, not a guarantee of daily runtime.

iPhone 18.note: No official Apple technical specifications page for the base iPhone 18 was available when this catalog was checked. Do not infer specifications from iPhone 18 Pro or earlier models.
